#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Cut the annotated tag + GitHub Release for the release bump that just landed
# on main (see auto_release.sh). Runs on the 'chore(release):' push to main —
# the `release-tag` job in ci.yml. Idempotent: an existing tag is a no-op.
# The tag is pushed with the fa-release-bot App token (checkout token,
# gh-1172) because GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger the tag-scoped
# binaries/publish jobs.
#
# gh-1192 AC3 — the tag pins the BUMP COMMIT, not moving main: the job's
# checkout can land on a main that advanced in the seconds between the bump
# push and this job starting (v1.0.498 captured the #1178 interloper that
# way), so BUMP_SHA — the push event's frozen head_commit.id — is passed by
# the workflow and validated (exact 'chore(release): v<ver>' subject + matching
# pubspec version) before use. A drifted/absent BUMP_SHA falls back to a
# history search for the bump commit; if neither resolves, the script REFUSES
# to tag rather than tag whatever HEAD points at.
set -euo pipefail

git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

git fetch origin main --tags --quiet
version=$(sed -n 's/^version: //p' pubspec.yaml)
tag="v$version"
if git rev-parse -q --verify "refs/tags/$tag^{commit}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "Tag $tag already exists — nothing to do."
  exit 0
fi

# ── Resolve the bump commit (gh-1192 AC3) ──────────────────────────────────
# A candidate qualifies only when its subject is exactly the bump subject AND
# its tree carries the tagged version — the two facts auto_release.sh authors
# into every bump commit. A drifted BUMP_SHA (github.sha can resolve to a
# newer main head) fails those checks and the history search decides instead.
resolve_bump() { # $1 = candidate sha; echoes the validated sha or nothing
  local candidate="$1" subject tree_version
  git cat-file -e "$candidate^{commit}" 2>/dev/null || return 1
  subject=[REDACTED:Certificate DN]
  tree_version=$(git show "$candidate":pubspec.yaml | sed -n 's/^version: //p')
  if [ "$subject" = "chore(release): v$version" ] && [ "$tree_version" = "$version" ]; then
    echo "$candidate"
  fi
}

bump_sha=""
if [ -n "${BUMP_SHA:-}" ]; then
  bump_sha=$(resolve_bump "$BUMP_SHA" || true)

# (the PR stopgap from 2026-09-29 is retired: it burned a full CI queue
    # cycle + machine review round on every chore bump). The App token is
    # minted job-locally; nothing else in the repo can read RELEASE_APP_*.
    # release-tag below cuts the tag from the pushed commit. Scheduled runs
    # catch up commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    # workflow_dispatch reaches this job ONLY through an explicit input gate
    # (gh-1172 round-2 BLOCK): this is the repo's dispatch-only CI — the SM
    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's
    # auto_release.sh with the bypass App's push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && !startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'chore(release):'))
      || github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true))
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the push rides the checkout
    # App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs write —
    # on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps the job's
    # own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # bypass credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (push, schedule, releaseDispatch) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): the App is the ruleset
          # bypass actor, so scope the token to what the push needs instead
          # of every permission the installation carries.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed commit triggers the
          # follow-up ci.yml run whose release-tag job cuts the tag —
          # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0

import re

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# protected main as the fa-release-bot GitHub App (gh-1172).

# Runs in CI on every push to main / the 2h catch-up cron / manual dispatch
# (the `release` job in .github/workflows/ci.yml). The job authenticates via
# actions/create-github-app-token (RELEASE_APP_ID + RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY);
# the App is the ONLY bypass actor on the main ruleset, so the bump commit
# pushes directly — no release PR, no machine review round-trip, no CI queue
# burn on a chore change. The tag + GitHub Release are still cut from the
# pushed 'chore(release):' commit by scripts/tag_release.sh (the `release-tag`
# job), riding the same App token so the tag-scoped binaries/publish jobs fire.
#
# Dry-run: RELEASE_DRY_RUN=1 (or "true") computes and commits the bump locally,
# logs the exact commit + tag that WOULD land, and skips the push.
#
# Changelog rules:
# - a curated `## Unreleased` section becomes the new version's notes;
# - otherwise notes are generated from commit subjects since the last tag;
# - a fresh empty `## Unreleased` is appended at the end (once — repeated runs
#   must not stack duplicates).
#
# Main-race honesty (E1): the push is fast-forward-only; a main that moved
# during the run rejects it and the retry loop re-computes from the fresh
# origin/main — never a blind push over new commits.
set -euo pipefail

# Commit authorship names the App so release commits are attributable in
# history (auditability contract, gh-1172).
git config user.name "fa-release-bot[bot]"
git config user.email "fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

dry_run=0
case "${RELEASE_DRY_RUN:-0}" in 1|true|yes) dry_run=1 ;; esac

# capped at one per 2h; runs with nothing new since the last tag are skipped.

    echo "Auto-release: nothing new since $last_tag, skipping."

  if [ "$tag_age" -lt 7200 ]; then
    echo "Auto-release: coalesced — $last_tag is ${tag_age}s old (<2h); $pending commit(s) pending. Next eligible push or the 2h cron will release them."
    exit 0
  fi

# the previous one would mis-tag the range. Keyed on the PUBSPEC VERSION, not

  if [ "$head_age" -lt 3600 ]; then
    echo "Auto-release: v$head_version pushed but untagged (release-tag job pending, ${head_age}s old) — skipping."

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Per-artifact uncompressed size manifest + budget gate (#1096 AC1).

Emits the per-entry uncompressed size table (the issue's inventory format)
for a shipped artifact and fails the build when any tracked line regresses
beyond the budget (default +5%).

Usage:
  size_manifest.py emit   <artifact> [--min-bytes N]        # TSV to stdout
  size_manifest.py check  <artifact> --baseline FILE
                          [--budget-pct 5] [--init-if-missing]
                          [--manifest-out FILE] [--forbid REGEX]...
  size_manifest.py selftest

`<artifact>` is a zip-family file (.zip/.ipa/.aab — uncompressed entry sizes
via zipfile) or a directory (tree of file sizes, for the web deploy root).

Manifest format (TSV; every row is `<bytes>\t<name>`, path-sorted. TOTAL
is an ordinary row — `<total_bytes>\tTOTAL` — and sorts among the paths;
do not rely on its position, the parser keys by name):
  <uncompressed_bytes>\t<path>
  <total_bytes>\tTOTAL

Gate semantics (`check`):
  - growth > budget%% on any baseline line or on TOTAL  -> FAIL
  - NEW line heavier than 5%% of the baseline TOTAL     -> FAIL
    (catches re-adding removed weight, e.g. a dropped interpreter coming
    back; canvaskit rev-dir churn on Flutter upgrades trips this too —
    that is by design: re-growth must be a conscious ack)
  - removed lines are improvements, reported only
  - --init-if-missing: no baseline file yet -> write it and pass with a
    loud notice (ratchet bootstrap; commit the file to arm the gate)
  - --reseed: overwrite an EXISTING baseline from this artifact and pass
    with a notice — the escape hatch for intentional growth; commit the
    rewritten file to make the new shape the floor
  - --forbid REGEX (repeatable): any manifest row whose path matches
    REGEX fails the check immediately, regardless of the +5% budget or
    the NEW-line share — the deny-list for evicted artifacts (a re-added
    5.6 MB fixture slips under both: NEW share is 5% of TOTAL). Enforced
    on check, --init-if-missing AND --reseed: re-admitting an artifact
    means dropping its --forbid flag, a conscious ack. The deny-list
    floor equals the tracking floor: sub-MIN_BYTES rows never enter the
    manifest.

CI escape hatch for intentional growth: re-run locally with the same
artifact and `--reseed`, commit the rewritten baseline.
"""

import argparse
import re

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Cut the annotated tag + GitHub Release for the release bump that just landed
# on main (see auto_release.sh). Runs on the 'chore(release):' push to main —
# the `release-tag` job in ci.yml. Idempotent: an existing tag is a no-op.
# The tag is pushed with the fa-release-bot App token (checkout token,
# gh-1172) because GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger the tag-scoped
# binaries/publish jobs.
#
# gh-1192 AC3 — the tag pins the BUMP COMMIT, not moving main: the job's
# checkout can land on a main that advanced in the seconds between the bump
# push and this job starting (v1.0.498 captured the #1178 interloper that
# way), so BUMP_SHA — the push event's frozen head_commit.id — is passed by
# the workflow and validated (exact 'chore(release): v<ver>' subject + matching
# pubspec version) before use. A drifted/absent BUMP_SHA falls back to a
# history search for the bump commit; if neither resolves, the script REFUSES
# to tag rather than tag whatever HEAD points at.
set -euo pipefail

git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

git fetch origin main --tags --quiet
version=$(sed -n 's/^version: //p' pubspec.yaml)
tag="v$version"
if git rev-parse -q --verify "refs/tags/$tag^{commit}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "Tag $tag already exists — nothing to do."
  exit 0
fi

# ── Resolve the bump commit (gh-1192 AC3) ──────────────────────────────────
# A candidate qualifies only when its subject is exactly the bump subject AND
# its tree carries the tagged version — the two facts auto_release.sh authors
# into every bump commit. A drifted BUMP_SHA (github.sha can resolve to a
# newer main head) fails those checks and the history search decides instead.
resolve_bump() { # $1 = candidate sha; echoes the validated sha or nothing
  local candidate="$1" subject tree_version
  git cat-file -e "$candidate^{commit}" 2>/dev/null || return 1

# (the PR stopgap from 2026-09-29 is retired: it burned a full CI queue
    # cycle + machine review round on every chore bump). The App token is
    # minted job-locally; nothing else in the repo can read RELEASE_APP_*.
    # release-tag below cuts the tag from the pushed commit. Scheduled runs
    # catch up commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    # workflow_dispatch reaches this job ONLY through an explicit input gate
    # (gh-1172 round-2 BLOCK): this is the repo's dispatch-only CI — the SM
    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's
    # auto_release.sh with the bypass App's push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && !startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'chore(release):'))
      || github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true))
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the push rides the checkout
    # App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs write —
    # on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps the job's
    # own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # bypass credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (push, schedule, releaseDispatch) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): the App is the ruleset
          # bypass actor, so scope the token to what the push needs instead
          # of every permission the installation carries.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed commit triggers the
          # follow-up ci.yml run whose release-tag job cuts the tag —
          # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:

The guard works — and it correctly flags the current repo CHANGELOG.md (263008 bytes ≥ cap). The 2 remaining failures are the repo-invariant tests (`repo CHANGELOG.md is under the cap` and possibly the archive sibling test) — these are the trim-dependent ones. Now do the trim (commit 1) to make them green.

Trim plan:
- `CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md` = header + sections before `## 1.0.506` (everything from original line 3 through the line before `## 1.0.506`).
- `CHANGELOG.md` = `# Changelog` + pointer note + `## 1.0.506` ... end (including `## Unreleased`).

Let me write the trim script carefully and verify the reassembly is lossless (archive body + kept body == original body).
The guard works and correctly flags the current 263 KB changelog. Now the trim — archive everything before `## 1.0.506` (keeping the last 30 versions inline):

{"command":"python3 - <<'PY'
import re
path = 'CHANGELOG.md'
text = open(path, encoding='utf-8').read()
matches = list(re.finditer(r'^## ', text, re.M))
KEEP = 30  # recent versions kept inline (ticket gh-1452: "last ~30 versions")
cut = matches[len(matches) - KEEP - 1].start()  # start of the window's first section

archived = text[cut:].rstrip('\n')          # nothing before it is dropped
kept = '# Changelog\n\n' + (
    'Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out\n'
    'on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose\n'
    'CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a\n'
    'bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` (release\n'
    'pre-tag + publish gates) fails fast when the cap is approached again.\n\n'
) + text[cut:].rstrip('\n') + '\n'
archive = (
    '# Changelog archive\n\n'
    'Entries before 1.0.506, moved out of `CHANGELOG.md` on 2026-10-09\n'
    '(gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose `CHANGELOG.md`\n'
    'exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so the inline file keeps a bounded\n'
    'recent window and this archive carries the tail. GitHub releases carry\n'
    'the same history per version.\n\n'
) + archived + '\n'

# Losslessness check: stripping both headers yields exactly the original body.
orig_body = text[text.index('\n', text.index('# Changelog')) + 1:]
new_body = kept[kept.index('## 1.0.506'):]
arch_body = archive[archive.index('## 0.1.397'):] if '## 0.1.397' in archive else archive[archive.index('## '):]
assert orig_body.strip() == (new_body.strip() if False else orig_body.strip())
combined = arch_body.rstrip('\n') + '\n' + new_body.rstrip('\n') + '\n'
assert combined == orig_body, (len(combined), len(orig_body))

open('CHANGELOG.md', 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(kept)
open('CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md', 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(archive)
print('kept bytes:', len(kept.encode()), 'archive bytes:', len(archive.encode()))
PY
wc -c CHANGELOG.md CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md; head -12 CHANGELOG.md; bash scripts/check_changelog_size.sh"}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Per-artifact uncompressed size manifest + budget gate (#1096 AC1).

Emits the per-entry uncompressed size table (the issue's inventory format)
for a shipped artifact and fails the build when any tracked line regresses
beyond the budget (default +5%).

Usage:
  size_manifest.py emit   <artifact> [--min-bytes N]        # TSV to stdout
  size_manifest.py check  <artifact> --baseline FILE
                          [--budget-pct 5] [--init-if-missing]
                          [--manifest-out FILE] [--forbid REGEX]...
  size_manifest.py selftest

`<artifact>` is a zip-family file (.zip/.ipa/.aab — uncompressed entry sizes
via zipfile) or a directory (tree of file sizes, for the web deploy root).

Manifest format (TSV; every row is `<bytes>\t<name>`, path-sorted. TOTAL
is an ordinary row — `<total_bytes>\tTOTAL` — and sorts among the paths;
do not rely on its position, the parser keys by name):
  <uncompressed_bytes>\t<path>
  <total_bytes>\tTOTAL

Gate semantics (`check`):
  - growth > budget%% on any baseline line or on TOTAL  -> FAIL
  - NEW line heavier than 5%% of the baseline TOTAL     -> FAIL
    (catches re-adding removed weight, e.g. a dropped interpreter coming
    back; canvaskit rev-dir churn on Flutter upgrades trips this too —
    that is by design: re-growth must be a conscious ack)
  - removed lines are improvements, reported only
  - --init-if-missing: no baseline file yet -> write it and pass with a
    loud notice (ratchet bootstrap; commit the file to arm the gate)
  - --reseed: overwrite an EXISTING baseline from this artifact and pass
    with a notice — the escape hatch for intentional growth; commit the
    rewritten file to make the new shape the floor
  - --forbid REGEX (repeatable): any manifest row whose path matches
    REGEX fails the check immediately, regardless of the +5% budget or
    the NEW-line share — the deny-list for evicted artifacts (a re-added
    5.6 MB fixture slips under both: NEW share is 5% of TOTAL). Enforced
    on check, --init-if-missing AND --reseed: re-admitting an artifact
    means dropping its --forbid flag, a conscious ack. The deny-list
    floor equals the tracking floor: sub-MIN_BYTES rows never enter the
    manifest.

CI escape hatch for intentional growth: re-run locally with the same
artifact and `--reseed`, commit the rewritten baseline.
"""

# the `release-tag` job in ci.yml. Idempotent: an existing tag is a no-op.
# The tag is pushed with the fa-release-bot App token (checkout token,
# gh-1172) because GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger the tag-scoped
# binaries/publish jobs.
#
# gh-1192 AC3 — the tag pins the BUMP COMMIT, not moving main: the job's
# checkout can land on a main that advanced in the seconds between the bump
# push and this job starting (v1.0.498 captured the #1178 interloper that
# way), so BUMP_SHA — the push event's frozen head_commit.id — is passed by
# the workflow and validated (exact 'chore(release): v<ver>' subject + matching
# pubspec version) before use. A drifted/absent BUMP_SHA falls back to a
# history search for the bump commit; if neither resolves, the script REFUSES
# to tag rather than tag whatever HEAD points at.
set -euo pipefail

git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

git fetch origin main --tags --quiet
version=$(sed -n 's/^version: //p' pubspec.yaml)
tag="v$version"
if git rev-parse -q --verify "refs/tags/$tag^{commit}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "Tag $tag already exists — nothing to do."
  exit 0
fi

# ── Resolve the bump commit (gh-1192 AC3) ──────────────────────────────────
# A candidate qualifies only when its subject is exactly the bump subject AND
# its tree carries the tagged version — the two facts auto_release.sh authors
# into every bump commit. A drifted BUMP_SHA (github.sha can resolve to a
# newer main head) fails those checks and the history search decides instead.
resolve_bump() { # $1 = candidate sha; echoes the validated sha or nothing
  local candidate="$1" subject tree_version
  git cat-file -e "$candidate^{commit}" 2>/dev/null || return 1
  subject=[REDACTED:Certificate DN]
  tree_version=$(git show "$candidate":pubspec.yaml | sed -n 's/^version: //p')
  if [ "$subject" = "chore(release): v$version" ] && [ "$tree_version" = "$version" ]; then
    echo "$candidate"
  fi
}

bump_sha=""
if [ -n "${BUMP_SHA:-}" ]; then
  bump_sha=$(resolve_bump "$BUMP_SHA" || true)
  if [ -z "$bump_sha" ]; then
    subject=[REDACTED:Certificate DN]
    echo "::warning::BUMP_SHA $BUMP_SHA is not the v$version bump (subject: $subject) — falling back to the history search"

fi

    bump_sha=$(resolve_bump "$candidate" || true)

# (the PR stopgap from 2026-09-29 is retired: it burned a full CI queue
    # cycle + machine review round on every chore bump). The App token is
    # minted job-locally; nothing else in the repo can read RELEASE_APP_*.
    # release-tag below cuts the tag from the pushed commit. Scheduled runs
    # catch up commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    # workflow_dispatch reaches this job ONLY through an explicit input gate
    # (gh-1172 round-2 BLOCK): this is the repo's dispatch-only CI — the SM
    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's
    # auto_release.sh with the bypass App's push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && !startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'chore(release):'))
      || github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true))
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the push rides the checkout
    # App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs write —
    # on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps the job's
    # own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # bypass credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (push, schedule, releaseDispatch) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): the App is the ruleset
          # bypass actor, so scope the token to what the push needs instead
          # of every permission the installation carries.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed commit triggers the
          # follow-up ci.yml run whose release-tag job cuts the tag —
          # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      # gh-1299 NG1: the bump regenerates flutter_app/pubspec.lock in-commit

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# CHANGELOG size guard (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
# CHANGELOG.md exceeds its hard content cap (262144 bytes) — v1.0.538 died at
# `dart publish` AFTER the tag + GitHub release existed, so the version
# never reached pub.dev. The changelog is append-only by convention and the
# auto-release grows it near-daily; nothing bounded it before this guard.

# Callers (keep both wired — test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart asserts them):

#   - ci.yml `publish` job gate   — BEFORE staging/upload (pre-upload fast-fail)

# Usage: check_changelog_size.sh [file] [cap_bytes]
#   file  defaults to CHANGELOG.md (the file pub packs)
#   cap   defaults to 262144 (the pub.dev cap); an override exists for tests
#
# Exit 0 = under the cap. Exit 1 = missing file or size >= cap, with a
# ::error:: annotation naming the fix (archive older entries).
set -euo pipefail

file="${1:-CHANGELOG.md}"
cap="${2:-262144}"

if [ ! -f "$file" ]; then
  echo "::error::check_changelog_size.sh: $file does not exist — a release without a changelog is a broken release (gh-1452)."

  exit 1
fi
echo "$file: $size bytes < $cap cap — ok"

    # auto_release.sh with the bypass App's push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && !startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'chore(release):'))
      || github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true))
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the push rides the checkout
    # App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs write —
    # on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps the job's
    # own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # bypass credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (push, schedule, releaseDispatch) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): the App is the ruleset
          # bypass actor, so scope the token to what the push needs instead
          # of every permission the installation carries.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed commit triggers the
          # follow-up ci.yml run whose release-tag job cuts the tag —
          # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Cut the annotated tag + GitHub Release for the release bump that just landed
# on main (see auto_release.sh). Runs on the 'chore(release):' push to main —
# the `release-tag` job in ci.yml. Idempotent: an existing tag is a no-op.
# The tag is pushed with the fa-release-bot App token (checkout token,
# gh-1172) because GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger the tag-scoped
# binaries/publish jobs.
#
# gh-1192 AC3 — the tag pins the BUMP COMMIT, not moving main: the job's
# checkout can land on a main that advanced in the seconds between the bump
# push and this job starting (v1.0.498 captured the #1178 interloper that
# way), so BUMP_SHA — the push event's frozen head_commit.id — is passed by
# the workflow and validated (exact 'chore(release): v<ver>' subject + matching
# pubspec version) before use. A drifted/absent BUMP_SHA falls back to a
# history search for the bump commit; if neither resolves, the script REFUSES
# to tag rather than tag whatever HEAD points at.

# (the PR stopgap from 2026-09-29 is retired: it burned a full CI queue
    # cycle + machine review round on every chore bump). The App token is
    # minted job-locally; nothing else in the repo can read RELEASE_APP_*.
    # release-tag below cuts the tag from the pushed commit. Scheduled runs
    # catch up commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    # workflow_dispatch reaches this job ONLY through an explicit input gate
    # (gh-1172 round-2 BLOCK): this is the repo's dispatch-only CI — the SM
    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's
    # auto_release.sh with the bypass App's push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && !startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'chore(release):'))
      || github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true))
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the push rides the checkout
    # App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs write —
    # on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps the job's
    # own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # bypass credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (push, schedule, releaseDispatch) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): the App is the ruleset
          # bypass actor, so scope the token to what the push needs instead
          # of every permission the installation carries.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed commit triggers the
          # follow-up ci.yml run whose release-tag job cuts the tag —
          # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0

    # release-tag below cuts the tag from the pushed commit. Scheduled runs

    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    # workflow_dispatch reaches this job ONLY through an explicit input gate
    # (gh-1172 round-2 BLOCK): this is the repo's dispatch-only CI — the SM
    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's
    # auto_release.sh with the bypass App's push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && !startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'chore(release):'))
      || github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true))
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the push rides the checkout
    # App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs write —
    # on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps the job's
    # own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # bypass credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"

      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0

{"content":"#!/usr/bin/env bash
# CHANGELOG size guard (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
# CHANGELOG.md exceeds its hard content cap — `Message from server:
# CHANGELOG.md exceeds the maximum content length (262144 bytes)`. v1.0.538
# died at `dart pub publish` AFTER the tag + GitHub release existed, so the
# version never reached pub.dev. The changelog is append-only by convention
# and the auto-release grows it near-daily; nothing bounded it before this
# guard.
#
# Callers (keep both wired — test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart asserts the
# wiring):
#   - scripts/auto_release.sh   — BEFORE the bump commit/tag (pre-tag
#     fast-fail: the push is what fires tag_release + the publish job);
#   - .github/workflows/ci.yml `publish` job gate — BEFORE staging/upload
#     (the server reject is the worst possible discovery point).
#
# Usage: check_changelog_size.sh [file] [cap_bytes]
#   file  defaults to CHANGELOG.md (the file pub packs);
#   cap   defaults to 262144 (the pub.dev cap) — strict less-than; the
#         override exists for tests.
#
# Exit 0 = under the cap. Exit 1 = missing file or size >= cap, with a
# ::error:: annotation naming the fix (archive the tail).
set -euo pipefail

file="${1:-CHANGELOG.md}"
cap="${2:-262144}"

if [ ! -f "$file" ]; then
  echo "::error::check_changelog_size.sh: $file does not exist — a release without a changelog is a broken release (gh-1452)."
  exit 1
fi

size=$(wc -c < "$file")
if [ "$size" -ge "$cap" ]; then
  echo "::error::$file is $size bytes — pub.dev rejects uploads at/over the ${cap}-byte content cap (gh-1452: v1.0.538 died mid-upload). Archive older entries to CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md (keep ~30 recent versions inline) and re-run the release."
  exit 1
fi
echo "$file: $size bytes < $cap-byte cap — ok"
","path":"scripts/check_changelog_size.sh"}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Cut the annotated tag + GitHub Release for the release bump that just landed
# on main (see auto_release.sh). Runs on the 'chore(release):' push to main —
# the `release-tag` job in ci.yml. Idempotent: an existing tag is a no-op.
# The tag is pushed with the fa-release-bot App token (checkout token,
# gh-1172) because GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger the tag-scoped
# binaries/publish jobs.
#
# gh-1192 AC3 — the tag pins the BUMP COMMIT, not moving main: the job's
# checkout can land on a main that advanced in the seconds between the bump
# push and this job starting (v1.0.498 captured the #1178 interloper that
# way), so BUMP_SHA — the push event's frozen head_commit.id — is passed by

# (the PR stopgap from 2026-09-29 is retired: it burned a full CI queue
    # cycle + machine review round on every chore bump). The App token is
    # minted job-locally; nothing else in the repo can read RELEASE_APP_*.
    # release-tag below cuts the tag from the pushed commit. Scheduled runs
    # catch up commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    # workflow_dispatch reaches this job ONLY through an explicit input gate
    # (gh-1172 round-2 BLOCK): this is the repo's dispatch-only CI — the SM
    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's
    # auto_release.sh with the bypass App's push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && !startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'chore(release):'))
      || github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true))
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the push rides the checkout
    # App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs write —
    # on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps the job's
    # own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # bypass credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (push, schedule, releaseDispatch) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): the App is the ruleset
          # bypass actor, so scope the token to what the push needs instead
          # of every permission the installation carries.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed commit triggers the
          # follow-up ci.yml run whose release-tag job cuts the tag —
          # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:

fi
echo "$file: $size bytes < $cap cap — ok"

Perhaps at some point the changelog was restructured/sorted differently, and later entries were appended at the end (ascending). Actually wait — maybe the head section (1.0.508, 1.0.485, 1.0.483, 1.0.472, 1.0.468, 1.0.457) is newest-first (descending), and then at some point it transitions to 0.1.397... ascending? That doesn't fit a simple pattern.

Hmm, 1.0.508 → 1.0.485 → 1.0.483 → 1.0.472 → 1.0.468 → 1.0.457 → 0.1.397 → 0.1.398 (ascending from there). So a descending run of 6 entries (508..457), then ascending 0.1.397 → 1.0.540? That's bizarre but whatever — the ordering doesn't matter much for my job: I need to keep "last ~30 versions". Since auto_release.sh APPENDS at the end (the `## Unreleased` handling appends new sections... wait no).

Let me look at auto_release.sh python: it looks for `## Unreleased` and replaces it with the new version section, then appends a fresh `## Unreleased` at the END. So new versions are added... let me think: `text = text[: m.start()] + new_section + ("\n" + tail if tail else "")`. The Unreleased section is at the END of the file (line 4828). So new sections REPLACE the Unreleased section in place — i.e., new entries are appended at the END of the file (after 1.0.540 comes Unreleased; next release: 1.0.541 replaces Unreleased in place, then a fresh Unreleased is appended at the end). So the changelog is effectively append-at-end (ascending) in its tail region.

So "last ~30 versions" = the last 30 `##` sections before `## Unreleased` (i.e., versions ~1.0.511..1.0.540), and archive everything before that.

Wait, but the head of the file has `## 1.0.508` first. Let me count the total number of version sections: 448 including Unreleased. Let me compute the byte size of the last 30 sections vs everything.

Let me write a small script to compute sizes. Also decide archive format:
- `CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md` gets everything older, with a header explaining it's the archive of older entries.
- `CHANGELOG.md` keeps `# Changelog` title + last ~30 version sections + `## Unreleased`.

The ticket says "keep a bounded recent window inline (e.g. last ~30 versions) and archive the tail to CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md (or drop it entirely — GitHub releases already carry full history). Target comfortably under 200 KiB."

    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    # workflow_dispatch reaches this job ONLY through an explicit input gate
    # (gh-1172 round-2 BLOCK): this is the repo's dispatch-only CI — the SM
    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's
    # auto_release.sh with the bypass App's push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && !startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'chore(release):'))
      || github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true))
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the push rides the checkout
    # App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs write —
    # on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps the job's
    # own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # bypass credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (push, schedule, releaseDispatch) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): the App is the ruleset
          # bypass actor, so scope the token to what the push needs instead
          # of every permission the installation carries.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed commit triggers the
          # follow-up ci.yml run whose release-tag job cuts the tag —
          # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

# (the PR stopgap from 2026-09-29 is retired: it burned a full CI queue
    # cycle + machine review round on every chore bump). The App token is
    # minted job-locally; nothing else in the repo can read RELEASE_APP_*.
    # release-tag below cuts the tag from the pushed commit. Scheduled runs
    # catch up commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    # workflow_dispatch reaches this job ONLY through an explicit input gate
    # (gh-1172 round-2 BLOCK): this is the repo's dispatch-only CI — the SM
    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's
    # auto_release.sh with the bypass App's push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && !startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'chore(release):'))
      || github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true))
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the push rides the checkout
    # App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs write —
    # on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps the job's
    # own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # bypass credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (push, schedule, releaseDispatch) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): the App is the ruleset
          # bypass actor, so scope the token to what the push needs instead
          # of every permission the installation carries.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed commit triggers the
          # follow-up ci.yml run whose release-tag job cuts the tag —
          # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0

fi
echo "$file: $size bytes < $cap cap — ok"

#   file  defaults to CHANGELOG.md (the file pub packs);
#   cap   defaults to 262144 (the pub.dev cap) — strict less-than; the
#         override exists for tests.
#
# Exit 0 = under the cap. Exit 1 = missing file or size >= cap, with a
# ::error:: annotation naming the fix (archive the tail).
set -euo pipefail

file="${1:-CHANGELOG.md}"
cap="${2:-262144}"

if [ ! -f "$file" ]; then
  echo "::error::check_changelog_size.sh: $file does not exist — a release without a changelog is a broken release (gh-1452)."
  exit 1
fi

size=$(wc -c < "$file")
if [ "$size" -ge "$cap" ]; then
  echo "::error::$file is $size bytes — pub.dev rejects uploads at/over the ${cap}-byte content cap (gh-1452: v1.0.538 died mid-upload). Archive older entries to CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md (keep ~30 recent versions inline) and re-run the release."
  exit 1
fi
echo "$file: $size bytes < $cap-byte cap — ok"

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg

    # release-tag below cuts the tag from the pushed commit. Scheduled runs
    # catch up commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    # workflow_dispatch reaches this job ONLY through an explicit input gate
    # (gh-1172 round-2 BLOCK): this is the repo's dispatch-only CI — the SM
    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's
    # auto_release.sh with the bypass App's push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && !startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'chore(release):'))
      || github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true))
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the push rides the checkout
    # App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs write —
    # on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps the job's
    # own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # bypass credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (push, schedule, releaseDispatch) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true

          # bypass actor, so scope the token to what the push needs instead

# CHANGELOG size guard (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
# CHANGELOG.md exceeds its hard content cap (262144 bytes) — v1.0.538 died at
# `dart publish` AFTER the tag + GitHub release existed, so the version

#   file  defaults to CHANGELOG.md (the file pub packs)
#   cap   defaults to 262144 (the pub.dev cap); an override exists for tests

# Exit 0 = under the cap. Exit 1 = missing file or size >= cap, with a
# ::error:: annotation naming the fix (archive older entries).
set -euo pipefail

file="${1:-CHANGELOG.md}"
cap="${2:-262144}"

if [ ! -f "$file" ]; then
  echo "::error::check_changelog_size.sh: $file does not exist — a release without a changelog is a broken release (gh-1452)."

  exit 1
fi
echo "$file: $size bytes < $cap cap — ok"

    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Cut the annotated tag + GitHub Release for the release bump that just landed

# gh-1172) because GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger the tag-scoped
# binaries/publish jobs.

# checkout can land on a main that advanced in the seconds between the bump
# push and this job starting (v1.0.498 captured the #1178 interloper that
# way), so BUMP_SHA — the push event's frozen head_commit.id — is passed by
# the workflow and validated (exact 'chore(release): v<ver>' subject + matching
# pubspec version) before use. A drifted/absent BUMP_SHA falls back to a
# history search for the bump commit; if neither resolves, the script REFUSES

git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

# (the PR stopgap from 2026-09-29 is retired: it burned a full CI queue
    # cycle + machine review round on every chore bump). The App token is
    # minted job-locally; nothing else in the repo can read RELEASE_APP_*.
    # release-tag below cuts the tag from the pushed commit. Scheduled runs
    # catch up commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    # workflow_dispatch reaches this job ONLY through an explicit input gate
    # (gh-1172 round-2 BLOCK): this is the repo's dispatch-only CI — the SM
    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's
    # auto_release.sh with the bypass App's push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && !startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'chore(release):'))
      || github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true))
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the push rides the checkout
    # App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs write —
    # on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps the job's
    # own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # bypass credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (push, schedule, releaseDispatch) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): the App is the ruleset
          # bypass actor, so scope the token to what the push needs instead
          # of every permission the installation carries.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

          fetch-depth: 0
          # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed commit triggers the

blocks.text:
# (the PR stopgap from 2026-09-29 is retired: it burned a full CI queue
    # cycle + machine review round on every chore bump). The App token is
    # minted job-locally; nothing else in the repo can read RELEASE_APP_*.
    # release-tag below cuts the tag from the pushed commit. Scheduled runs
    # catch up commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    # workflow_dispatch reaches this job ONLY through an explicit input gate
    # (gh-1172 round-2 BLOCK): this is the repo's dispatch-only CI — the SM
    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's
    # auto_release.sh with the bypass App's push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && !startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'chore(release):'))
      || github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true))
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the push rides the checkout
    # App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs write —
    # on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps the job's
    # own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # bypass credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (push, schedule, releaseDispatch) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): the App is the ruleset
          # bypass actor, so scope the token to what the push needs instead
          # of every permission the installation carries.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed commit triggers the
          # follow-up ci.yml run whose release-tag job cuts the tag —
          # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

# (the PR stopgap from 2026-09-29 is retired: it burned a full CI queue
    # cycle + machine review round on every chore bump). The App token is
    # minted job-locally; nothing else in the repo can read RELEASE_APP_*.
    # release-tag below cuts the tag from the pushed commit. Scheduled runs
    # catch up commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    # workflow_dispatch reaches this job ONLY through an explicit input gate
    # (gh-1172 round-2 BLOCK): this is the repo's dispatch-only CI — the SM
    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's
    # auto_release.sh with the bypass App's push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && !startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'chore(release):'))
      || github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true))
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the push rides the checkout
    # App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs write —
    # on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps the job's
    # own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # bypass credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (push, schedule, releaseDispatch) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): the App is the ruleset
          # bypass actor, so scope the token to what the push needs instead
          # of every permission the installation carries.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed commit triggers the
          # follow-up ci.yml run whose release-tag job cuts the tag —
          # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
